headline: Staff Platform Engineer. Agentic AI, full-stack and AI security on AWS. AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional.
summary: I've been building software, cloud platforms and distributed systems for 19 years, more than ten of them on AWS. In Commonwealth Bank's AI Centre of Excellence I turn unclear generative AI and data problems into secure production systems. Before that I was an AWS consultant at Cevo, working inside enterprise client teams, and before that I spent nine years as founder and CTO of a software consultancy that grew to 40 people, writing code and selling the work myself.
Most of my recent projects started as unclear briefs spread across several teams, so the first job was working out what was actually needed. I still write a lot of the code myself.

experience.role: Staff Platform Engineer (MLOps), AI Centre of Excellence
points: Technical anchor for a data-lineage platform from early design to production: backend architecture, authentication, deployment readiness and production debugging across software, data and infrastructure teams.

Narrowed a very broad lineage brief to the three journeys data stewards needed most, then built a security-reviewed prototype with AWS engineers in three weeks. Later showed an enriched Amazon Neptune lineage graph with 113,000 nodes and 146,000 edges.

Designed hybrid lineage extraction: deterministic Python parsers for known job-schedule, JCL and SQL patterns, with a schema-constrained LLM fallback for edge cases. People ask lineage questions in plain English and can trace answers back to the source code and metadata.
Set up workload-identity and OAuth 2.0 patterns for service-to-service and agent-to-tool access, and scoped the security assessments and pen tests behind APRA and internal risk reviews.

Raised the squad's DevSecOps maturity score from 1.81 to 2.75 in one cycle by tying 14 controls to delivery goals: versioned prompts, LLM-judge evaluation, SAST, DAST and SCA, and staged deploys with rollback.
Ran authorised prompt-injection testing of an internal multi-agent assistant, which led to guardrail work in the team. Mentored engineers and ran internal talks on authentication patterns.

experience.role: Tech Lead, AWS and generative AI (AI medical scribe)
points: Built the AWS foundation for patient health data: multi-account setup with Control Tower, SCPs and least-privilege IAM, KMS key rotation, encryption in transit and at rest, and CI/CD on GitHub Actions with OIDC.

Standard guardrails were distorting sensitive clinical content, so I replaced free-form note generation with two-pass structured extraction where each statement cites the transcript lines it came from. LLM-as-judge evaluation and prompt versioning let us measure prompt changes across models.

experience.role: AWS Cloud Consultant, embedded with enterprise clients
points: Development lead for regulated Consumer Data Right REST APIs at a large energy provider. Led the domain-API and data-integration teams (8 engineers) and built the AWS data platform behind them.
Fixed a production outage the same day on Amazon Neptune and Gremlin, a stack I learned on the spot. The fix became a bounded-query pattern used across all endpoints.
Found accounts with far more transactions than a 10,000-result limit allowed and moved the design to paged queries. Drafted the team's definition of done.

In June 2023, proposed disposable cloud dev environments where an AI agent picks up a ticket and hands back its plan and a pull request for review, plus a self-hosted coding assistant so source code stays in-house.

For a client that wanted a custom SageMaker build, ran discovery across three departments, then built a serverless prototype overnight with SES, S3, Step Functions, Textract, Comprehend and Bedrock. The design that went ahead needed no model training and cost very little to run.
Delivered production retrieval over a very large legacy SharePoint estate with Amazon Q Business.

experience.role: Founder and CTO, Principal Solutions Architect
points: Started the company and grew it to 40 people across two countries. Ran sales myself, from technical discovery to proposals and pricing, and delivered 80+ engagements, mostly web and cloud applications for universities, archives, international organisations and companies.
Designed an access-controlled archive platform on AWS for thousands of recorded testimonies. Built an e-signature product from scratch on Java/Spring, S3 and SQS that was later acquired.
Co-built an open-source archival management system (millions of records, a million hours of media) and a misinformation-monitoring platform. Wrote the engineering playbook.

Power cuts kept costing developers their work, so I moved development into the browser: each developer got a VS Code environment from a project template, shut down when idle. It started on one rented server shared by 12 developers and later moved to Firecracker and Cloud Hypervisor microVMs.

experience.role: Senior Software Engineer, then Co-Partner and CTO

projects: An AWS Professional Services-style team modelled as GPT-4 agents. They scope an architecture brief and check the plan against the Well-Architected Framework, and once a person approves it, an engineer agent drafts the code.

Open-source Claude Code plugin where a supervisor coordinates sub-agents from planning through test-first development and review, each task in its own git worktree. Nothing runs until I approve the plan. Also agent-handoff, a Go tool for passing decisions between agent sessions.
Working-draft open spec for packaging AI agents. An Agentfile declares what an agent needs and builds into OCI image labels a platform can enforce with Cedar. Reference CLI in Go.
React prototype for designing an agent system, from MCP tools and guardrails to synthetic training data and fine-tuning cost estimates.
Extended a Next.js, Prisma and PostgreSQL CRM with Google Workspace integrations and an MCP-based assistant. Built an exam-prep app on Tauri v2 and SQLite.
Reported AI security issues through responsible disclosure (2024). A fix to OpenWrt's luci-app-trafficctl was merged upstream (Aug 2026).
skills: Python, Java, Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, Ruby, PHP; C#/.NET earlier on.
REST APIs, microservices, event-driven workflows (SQS, Step Functions), Spring, Rails, Node.js; PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Amazon Neptune (Gremlin), OpenSearch.

Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Q Business, MCP, multi-agent orchestration (AutoGen, LangChain); RAG with hybrid retrieval and reranking, embeddings, pgvector, FAISS, Qdrant; prompt versioning, LLM-as-judge evaluation, guardrails; OpenAI API since June 2021.
Claude Code, OpenCode; sub-agents, hooks and test-first gates; author of Claude Code plugins.
Lambda, ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, Docker, S3, RDS, IAM, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, Control Tower; CloudFormation, Terraform, Pulumi; GitHub Actions, GitLab CI; Firecracker, Proxmox.
OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, JWT, SAML, workload identity, Cedar; SAST, DAST, SCA; prompt-injection testing; APRA, HIPAA, CDR.
